title: Like grandfather, like grandson
odia:
ଅଜା ଜାଣି ନାତି
ମାଛ ଜାଣି କାତି।
literal_meaning: As the grandfather, so the grandson; as the fish, so its scales.
meaning_odia: ଅଜାଙ୍କ ସହ ନାତିର ମେଳକୁ ମାଛ ଓ ତାହାର କାତିର ମେଳ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏଠାରେ ପରିବାରର ଜଣକ ଭିତରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଲକ୍ଷଣ ଦେଖାଯିବାର କଥା ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The parallel pairs suggest a likeness: the grandson takes after his grandfather, just as the scales belong to the kind of fish that bears them. This is an editorial reading of the comparison. The lines name no particular good or bad trait.
usage_example: A grandson tells a story with the same gestures and mischievous smile as his grandfather. Someone watching might recall these lines. This example is newly composed.
cultural_context: ଅଜା denotes the maternal grandfather, and ନାତି a grandson. The family comparison is paired with the visible covering of a fish: କାତି is read here as scales. The image suggests resemblance without establishing that character is fixed by ancestry.

graphic.alt: An older man and a child mirror each other's hand gestures while a group watches; a fish drawing lies on the mat.
graphic.caption: An imagined shared gesture evokes resemblance between generations without fixing anyone’s character by ancestry.

odia_summary: ମାଛ ସହ କାତିର ଯେପରି ମେଳ, ଅଜାଙ୍କ ସହ ନାତିର ସେପରି ମେଳ।
english_summary: A grandson’s resemblance to his grandfather is pictured through a fish and its scales.
